- These targets are proposals. Only the extra-entry costs above were measured; the fall in rows is not predicted.

### B. The checker is scheduled by the props that will be shown

The owner asked for a queue. Its parts, against what exists:

- **Item.** The props of one component that relevance will show, at one revision, not the whole component; collapsed members are listed by name and parent and never converted. Exists: `SemanticTarget::react_wanted` and `described` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:169-175`) already narrow what one target converts. New: a `shown` set from `relevance::decide`.
- **Priority classes**, on-screen > neighbouring stories > background fill. Exists: two (`Priority::Interactive` and `Background`, `types/semantic.rs:221`), two lanes with a starvation bound and raising (`Queue`, `on_demand.rs:150-199`, `INTERACTIVE_STREAK` 4), a raise when an on-screen request joins a queued one (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:256`). The addon's prefetch queue holds the next `prefetchStories - 1` stories, replaced on every selection (`packages/storybook/src/background.ts:39`, `preset.ts:150`, `prefetch.ts:32`), one story at a time (`background.ts:81-89`), and asks at `Background` (`pipeline/watch.rs:464`). New: a third class, `Neighbour`, between them.
- **Preemption and cancel.** Exists: an edit forgets every kept and pending answer in the hook (`semantic_hook.rs:180`); the lifecycle reducer refreshes an answer superseded by an edit (`lifecycle.ts:196`); navigation replaces the addon's queue. Missing: nothing reaches `OnDemand`'s queue, which has no cancel, so requests nobody waits for still run. New: a request carries a cancel token tripped by an edit or by the navigation that replaced it, dropped when taken. Raising a request clears its token: an on-screen request that joined a queued prefetch (`Found::Joined`, `semantic_hook.rs:256`) is waited for, so a navigation never cancels it; and preemption between components of one request (a tsrs call cannot be interrupted).
- **Batching by snapshot.** Exists: `OnDemand` keeps one snapshot and re-roots it per request (`Checker::snapshot_for`, `on_demand.rs:551`); the one-shot CLI answers every component on one program with eight files in flight sharing one converter (`crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:49`, `session`). A request whose roots differ re-roots the snapshot (`rerooted`, `on_demand.rs:574`), which makes a new one with new type ids. New: the worker takes the queued items of one class together and roots one snapshot at the union of their roots, so they share the program and one converter memo; the memo is dropped with that snapshot, never carried to an updated or re-rooted one (type ids are valid within one snapshot, ADR 0026). The memo is per request today.
- **Admission on a memory budget.** Exists: the arena guard (`Upkeep::decide`, `on_demand.rs:709`), which misses the converter heap. In flight: the one-shot heap budget (heap-budget slice B, branch `feat/one-shot-heap-budget`, no commits yet), counting converted nodes inside conversion. New: the scheduler admits a background item only under a soft budget read from the allocator, holds background work above it, and stops the checker above the hard one, as `stop_past_bound` does.
- **Stream each result.** Exists: one `Delivery` per request (`types/semantic.rs:256`), and the reducer turns each settled key into a refresh (`lifecycle.ts:185-205`, invariants 1 to 6). New: a request of several keys delivers each key when converted. The CLI keeps one write: canonical JSON interns props across components (ADR 0009, 0018).

Not determined: whether tsrs's memory allows the converter memo to live as long as a snapshot over a long session (ADR 0026 measured 98 to 246 MB over 150 edits without it); whether `mi_process_info` reads the same under the napi host; how far listing collapsed members without converting them lowers the 42 GB case, since the collapse PR collapses `SystemProperties` after conversion.

## Consequences

# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct
# suite through the checker path (the release binary, which links tsrs) held to checker-expectations.json; see
# apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md.
test-checker-lane:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity
    CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec vitest run tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts
    # S5's gate on tsrs: generic components instantiated.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib instantiate
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test instantiate
    # S6's gate on tsrs: a kept snapshot brought up to date, and an edit nobody announced caught loudly.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test watch
    # The built-in checker's stack holds a type 10,000 deep without aborting its host (trail 369): release only.
    cargo test --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib a_type_nested_ten_thousand_deep -- --ignored --exact checker::tests::a_type_nested_ten_thousand_deep_is_printed_in_full

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

# Measure ADR 0026's memory, determinism, first-answer and watch gates on the built-in checker, as the addon runs it
# (docs/gate-measurements.md). Builds the large project outside the repository (GATE_FIXTURES, default

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summaries and writes each package's coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/*.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src/**/*.ts' 'apps/oracle/tests/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src' 'packages/storybook/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests' 'packages/storybook/tests' 'apps/oracle/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    node scripts/check-packaging.mjs
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check

# Everything the CI jobs run, minus the Node version matrix and verify-install
ci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete semver msrv (coverage "90")

cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API of every published library crate for SemVer breaks against the last published version.
# The version only moves in the release PR, so a break is accepted when a pending minor or major changeset covers the
# crate. The CLI crate is a binary and has no library API.
semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    status=0
    for crate in caliper-docgen-core caliper-docgen-semantic; do
        if cargo semver-checks check-release -p "$crate"; then
            continue
        fi
        if grep -qsE "^cargo/$crate: (minor|major)$" .changeset/*.md; then
            echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for $crate"
            continue
        fi
        echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/$crate" >&2
        status=1
    done
    exit "$status"

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`

# Check the public Rust API of every published library crate for SemVer breaks against the last published version.
# The version only moves in the release PR, so a break is accepted when a pending minor or major changeset covers the
# crate. The CLI crate is a binary and has no library API.
semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    status=0
    for crate in caliper-docgen-core caliper-docgen-semantic; do
        if cargo semver-checks check-release -p "$crate"; then
            continue
        fi
        if grep -qsE "^cargo/$crate: (minor|major)$" .changeset/*.md; then
            echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for $crate"
            continue
        fi
        echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/$crate" >&2
        status=1
    done
    exit "$status"

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

The on-demand checker answers in three classes: the story shown first, then the stories next to it, then warm-up and fill work, in arrival order within each. A queued request nobody waits for is dropped before the checker converts it when an edit supersedes the revision it was asked at, or when the client no longer shows its component; a request already being converted finishes. For library users: `Priority` has a new `Neighbour` variant, `SharedPriority` gains `raise_to`, `cancel` and `is_cancelled`, and `WatchSession` gains `components_as_neighbours` and `cancel_components`. A caller that names no priority is answered as before.

input.content:
## What

ADR 0028 S1, classes and cancel (trail 405, wave 1). Stacked on #476 (`feat/skip-converting-collapsed-layer-props`).

- `Priority` gets a third class, `Neighbour`, between `Interactive` and `Background`. It is ordered (`Ord`): the lesser value is answered first.
- `SharedPriority` holds the class and a cancel bit. It has new methods `raise_to(priority)`, `cancel()` and `is_cancelled()`. `raise()` is still `raise_to(Interactive)`. Raising a request clears its cancel bit. `cancel()` does nothing to an `Interactive` request: someone waits for it.
- `OnDemand`'s `Queue` keeps one arrival-ordered deque. The next request is the oldest of the first class waiting. A request raised while it waits is filed again behind the requests already in its new class, as before. When the next request is picked, cancelled requests are dropped first. Their `Delivery` gets `None` and they are never converted. A request the worker already took is not interrupted, because a tsrs call cannot be. The starvation bound (`INTERACTIVE_STREAK`, 4) now covers three classes: after a run of 4 picks from the first class while a lesser class waits, the oldest lesser request goes next. A run counts one class only.
- Hook: `invalidate` (an edit) cancels every pending request nobody waits for, since its answer would not be kept. `SemanticHook::cancel(keys)` cancels pending non-interactive requests for those keys and removes them from the join map, so a later caller asks again. When a request settles as cancelled, the caller is told the answer is pending, never that the checker stopped. A joiner raises the pending request to its own class (`raise_to`).
- `WatchSession::components_as_neighbours(keys)` asks at `Neighbour` without waiting. `WatchSession::cancel_components(keys)` is for S2, which calls it when a prefetch queue is replaced.
- A caller that names no priority is unchanged: `request` still asks at `Interactive`, the default `request_at` ignores priority and never drops a request, and the CLI one-shot path is untouched.
- Changeset: core minor (new enum variant and new methods, which `just semver` flags; a pending minor covers it), semantic patch.

## Evidence

- New tests:
  - `a_neighbour_request_goes_after_an_on_screen_one_and_before_a_fill`: the ADR's first test.
  - `a_cancelled_request_is_never_answered`: the ADR's second test.
  - `a_request_raised_while_it_waits_goes_with_its_new_class`
  - `a_waiting_lesser_request_goes_after_a_bounded_run_of_the_first_class`
  - `a_run_of_one_class_does_not_count_toward_the_next_classes_run`
  - `a_request_for_a_component_nobody_shows_is_dropped_before_conversion`
  - `a_request_of_a_superseded_revision_is_dropped`
  - `a_cancelled_request_is_not_reported_as_a_stopped_checker`
- The queue tests run in `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs`. The hook and session tests run in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs` with a holding fake checker. Each fails on the base: the variant and methods do not exist there.
- The existing queue and join tests pass unchanged, including `semantic_join.rs` and `a_story_asked_behind_queued_background_requests_is_answered_before_them`.
- nextest for core, semantic and cli (`caliper-docgen`): 1492 passed, 2 skipped, exit 0.
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0. Construct check: 254 fixtures, 0 differ. Parity: 254 identical.
- `just semver`: exit 0.
- Identity diff of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` with the checker on, `stats` dropped, base ref `2b182681` against this branch:
  - gate-large: IDENTICAL, 4,938,806 bytes
  - chakra-only: IDENTICAL, 2,432,715 bytes
  - shadcn-ui (`apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui`): IDENTICAL, 1,887,510 bytes
  - mantine core (`packages/@mantine/core/src`): IDENTICAL, 57,187,685 bytes
  - All exits were 0. The diff ran before and after the review round.
- `gate_harness determinism` on gate-large (built-in tsc): exit 0. `gate_harness memory`: exit 0. Both ran before and after the review round.
- `/code-review medium` (one round). Fixed:
  - A cancelled request was reported as "the TypeScript checker stopped". It now settles as `Settled::Cancelled`, which the caller reads as pending.
  - The streak carried over from one class's run to the next.
  - A doc line ran past 120 columns.

## Not verified

- Production wiring is S2's job. Nothing outside tests calls `components_as_neighbours` or `cancel_components` yet, and the addon still prefetches at `Background`.
- Review findings left open:
  - `cancel` removes the pending entry even when the worker is already converting it. If the client navigates back, a second request is queued behind the first: duplicate work, but not a wrong answer. The hook cannot see whether the worker took the request.
  - An `Interactive` request is never cancelled, even after its waiter timed out. This follows the ADR ("raising clears its token … a navigation never cancels it").
  - An edit now drops the warm-up and fill requests still queued, and nothing queues them again. Before this change they ran, but their answers were already discarded by the generation check. The only thing lost is the side effect of warming the checker's snapshot.
  - `Queue::next` rebuilds the deque on each pick, which is O(n) per pick. Next to a conversion this is negligible, and no measurement was made.
  - On a starvation turn, a request raised from Background to Neighbour can lose its turn to an older Background request. A raised request counts as filed when it was raised.
  - The new hook tests repeat part of the `tests/semantic_join.rs` harness, and their spin wait has no timeout, like `Queued::wait_until`. They stay in owned files.
- To run its pnpm gates, the worktree needed `pnpm install --offline --ignore-scripts` and a `target/release` link to the private target directory. Before that, 28 cli config and core snapshot tests failed: the cli tests could not find `tsx` and the snapshots resolved `@types/react` from the parent checkout. All of them passed after the install.
